american-standard.notes: Reuse evidence comes from the Trane page, NOT from this page: the Trane page labels the year-first system as a Trane (American Standard) style begun in 2002, states it remains in use under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names, and states the older styles continued in use for many years under the Ingersoll Rand, American Standard, Trane and GE names. CAVEAT: the American Standard page itself contains history only and no serial-number decoding section, so sister-page confirmation is unavailable; if the project requires sister-page confirmation strictly, hold this file as a gap instead of shipping reuse. No parent company is stated on the American Standard page, so parent is omitted.

styles.era: 2010-present, digit-led serials (page Style 1, later form)
styles.notes: Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2010+ reading) and style-1 (2002-2009 reading); this style is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading. The page notes the styles overlap and directs techs to the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate; a 2002 serial in the overlap set will decode as a 2020s year.

styles.era: 2002-2009, digit-led serials (page Style 1, early form)
styles.notes: Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2002-2009 reading) and style-2 (2010+ reading); style-2 is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate per the page. A 2002 serial in the overlap set therefore decodes as a 2020s year; this is a documented page ambiguity, not a silent guess.

styles.era: 1983-2001, letter-led 9-character serials (page Style 2)
styles.notes: Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: page text says letters A, I, L, O and Q were not used, yet the standard chart reading (corroborated by three independent sources) gives L = 1996; L = 1996 is included pending visual chart verification. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Page states the 4th position encodes month but gives no letter-to-month table (the documented example's 4th character is M), so month is not encoded. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.

bryant.notes: BDP system. Sister Payne shares styles 1-4 in shape, positions, era, and example serials. The page also lists Aquazone, BDP, Day and Night, and Weathermaster as related brands, but their serial systems were not verified in this batch and are not claimed as shared. Carrier is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not claimed as sharing this system. Style 3 Canada reverses year/month positions vs US. Single-digit years in styles 3, 3-Canada, and 4 are encoded as digit-keyed letterTable maps because the schema digits kind does not support 1-character year slices; the mappings themselves are fully documented on the page. Schema-prose note: the locked schema says letterTable keys must be single uppercase letters; digit keys work in the builder (JSON keys are strings, table lookup is exact) but a future schema clarification (digitTable kind or prose update) should ratify this.

styles.era: 10-character format, week-year in first four digits
styles.notes: Week is 1st-2nd positions, year is 3rd-4th positions. Week decode for the example is 07.

styles.era: Primarily 1980s, 9-digit all-numeric
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd positions, month is 3rd-4th positions.

styles.era: 1980-1984, US systems
styles.notes: Month letter is 1st position, M-Z skipping O and U for January-December. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-4 for 1980-1984. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

styles.era: 1980-1984, Canadian systems (positions reversed vs US)
styles.notes: Canadian variant only: year digit is 1st position, month letter is 2nd position, same tables as US style 3. Split from style 3 because one style cannot carry two position assignments.

Month letter is 1st position, A-L with no letters skipped. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-9 for 1970-1979. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

styles.era: 1960-1979, two-digit week prefix
styles.notes: Year letter begins with L for 1960 and cycles to H for 1979, skipping O, Q, and Z. Week is the 1st-2nd positions; the example week is 46. Split from the one-digit-week variant because fixed position ranges cannot express both.

styles.era: 1960-1979, one-digit week prefix
styles.notes: Same year-letter table as style 5a. Week is the 1st position only; the example week is 2.

coleman.notes: Coleman does NOT use usesStylesOf york: styles 1-2 match York's systems verbatim (same sample serials, same letter tables, same October 2004 boundary, charts note York UPG manufacturing), but styles 3-4 are Coleman-only numeric systems and the builder forbids styles alongside usesStylesOf. The month/year order swap is documented as a 1991/1992 boundary, not April 1992: style 4 (month first) ended 1991, style 3 (year first) began 1992. Dual-brand Coleman-Evcon history 1999-2005 is documented on the page. HELD, NOT SHIPPED (schema blockers, see below): style-1 (after October 2004, 10-character serials, sample W0K5896070 = September 2005) splits its year digits around the month letter (2nd and 4th characters), which the locked schema cannot express with a single contiguous slice; style-2 (1971 to October 2004, 4 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample WAKM011379 = January 1980 or 2001) repeats its year letters on a 21-year cycle (A-N map to two years each) with no documented disambiguator. Shipping a first-cycle-only year table would silently mis-decode 1992-2004 units, so neither style is shipped until the schema gains multi-range positions and dual-candidate year handling.

styles.era: From 1992 (9-digit numeric serials)
styles.notes: Year first, month second. yearFloor 1992 reflects the documented start year; with this floor, trying style-3 before style-4 resolves the numeric overlap: a 9-digit serial whose style-3 month field is invalid falls through to style-4, and a serial matching style-3 with year 1992 or later cannot be a style-4 serial (style-4 ended 1991).

styles.era: Prior to 1992, ended 1991 (numeric serials)
styles.notes: Month first, year second: the reverse of style-3. DOCUMENTED-LENGTH DISCREPANCY: the page's style list shows a 9-digit sample (018812345) but the style-4 chart body shows 10 digits (0188123456, month 01, year 88, 6-digit sequence); the 10-digit body serial is used as the example and the pattern allows 9-10 digits. RESIDUAL EDGE, flagged not resolved: a 9-digit serial that fails style-3 month validation but passes style-4 with a year of 1992 or later would decode to a post-1991 year outside style-4's documented era; the schema has no era upper bound to reject it. No start date is documented for this style, so the default 1960 floor is kept.

daikin.notes: Only 3 of the page's 10 styles encode as deterministic serial rules from the page text: page styles 2, 7 and 10. Page style 1 carries no serial encoding (year and month read only from the printed manufacture-date label) and is not encoded. Page styles 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 decode through charts shown only as images on the page; the chart contents are not recoverable from the page text, so no tables are encoded for them and they are held as gaps pending a read of the chart images. Related brands Goodman, Amana and Janitrol are listed on the page but use their own serial systems; no styles are copied from them and usesStylesOf is null. Two-digit years resolve by the schema century rule with floor 1960. Example decodes are derived mechanically from the page's documented positions (the page states positions, not manufactured-in sentences, for these three styles).

styles.era: Page style 2: 4-letter prefix followed by 10 digits
styles.notes: Page style 2: year is the 5th and 6th characters (first two digits after the 4-letter prefix), month is the 7th and 8th characters. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 09 -> 2009, 05 -> May.

styles.era: Page style 7: 1 letter followed by 9 digits
styles.notes: Page style 7: year is the 2nd and 3rd digits, week is the 4th and 5th digits. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 88 -> 1988, week 12.

styles.era: Page style 10: 10-digit numeric serials
styles.notes: Page style 10: year is the 1st and 2nd numbers, month is the 3rd and 4th numbers. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 16 -> 2016, 02 -> February.

goodman.notes: Style 1 is the 10-digit numeric system (fully validated). Style 2 (select PTAC systems manufactured for Goodman by Daikin Industries, serials ending in P or D, ended shortly after the 2012 Daikin acquisition) is NOT encoded: the page documents its letter positions (year = 3rd position / 2nd letter, month = 2nd position / 1st letter) and its example serial 5FU5472618P, but gives no letter-to-year or letter-to-month mapping in retrievable text and no stated decode for that example, so no Style 2 table is shipped rather than guessed. Amana is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not listed as a sister sharing this system and has no file (documented gap). The style list variant 9704 011000 shares Style 1's YYMM prefix but has no separately stated decode, so it is not added as an example.

styles.era: 10-digit numeric serials
styles.notes: Page positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month (1-based), converted to 0-based half-open ranges. Page example shown as 97 04811080.

janitrol.notes: Legacy brand: acquired by Goodman circa 1982, brand name discontinued in 1992; kept as its own file per the legacy pass-through rule, not merged into Goodman. Reuse evidence is page-framing only: the Janitrol page is headed Janitrol-Goodman-GmC-Amana and frames age determination as Goodman Manufacturing brand systems, with Goodman Manufacturing Company, L.P. as parent. The page gives no Janitrol-specific positions, formats, or examples, so this reuse rests on that framing, not on position-level confirmation on the Janitrol page.

styles.era: 10-digit numeric serials
styles.notes: Page positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month (1-based), converted to 0-based half-open ranges. Page example shown as 97 04811080.

keeprite.notes: ICP system. Styles 1-3 are identical to Tempstar styles 1-3 in example serials, shapes, and positions. NOT usesStylesOf Tempstar because Tempstar lists an additional style 6 that the Keeprite page does not list; verbatim reuse would add an unverified style to Keeprite. HELD GAPS — style 4 (8-digit numeric, year = 1st digit, week = 2nd-3rd digits): format example only, year mapping chart-image-only; style 5 (letter-digit-letter prefix, year = 3rd letter): placeholder only, year-letter chart image-only, tail shape undocumented. Neither is shipped rather than guessed.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits
styles.notes: Year is 2nd-3rd digits, week is 4th-5th digits. Week decode for the example is 16.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits, with printed MFG date on tag
styles.notes: Page states this serial is identical in system to style 1; the printed MFG date 2/92 corroborates year 1992 and week 06. Pattern and positions duplicate style 1, so this style never wins first-match, but its decode is identical.

styles.era: 10-character format, year-week in first four digits
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd digits, week is 3rd-4th digits. Week decode for the example is 14.

lennox.notes: Page lists related brands (AirEase, Airease-Johnson, Aire-flo, Allied-Commercial, Allied, Armstrong Air, Concord, Ducane, Magic-Pak, Advanced Distributor Products (ADP), Heatcraft) but does not document that any shares this serial system, so no sisters or usesStylesOf are set. Page presents pre-1973 serials as a single style with a 1- or 2-digit month; split here into two file styles because schema positions are fixed ranges. Two-digit years resolve by the schema century rule with the default 1960 floor, so pre-1960 pre-1973 serials return cannot-determine rather than a guessed year. The page documents only one month-letter system (A-M minus I, 1973+); there are no separate month-letter eras to encode.

styles.era: 1973 and after, 10-character serials
Prior to 1973, 3-character serials (1-digit month)
Prior to 1973, 4-character serials (2-digit month)

luxaire.notes: Luxaire does NOT use usesStylesOf york: it has extra numeric and 2-letter styles, and its style-1 month table conflicts with York's for September-December (see held-style note). HELD, NOT SHIPPED: style-1 (10-character serials, sample W0K5896070) splits its year digits around the month letter, which the locked schema cannot express with a single contiguous slice; it also carries a MONTH-TABLE CONFLICT: Luxaire's own style-1 chart maps K to October (J September, L November, M December, no N), while the York and Coleman charts map the same sample serial's K to September (K September, L October, M November, N December) — the same serial decodes to September 2005 on York/Coleman but October 2005 on Luxaire, and only a real data-plate check can settle it, so Luxaire's table must not be overwritten with York's on suspicion. Styles 4 (4 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample WAKM011379 = January 1980 or 2001) and 5 (2 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample HM409295 = August 1982 or 2003) repeat their year letters on a 21-year cycle with no documented disambiguator and are likewise held; style-4's month table (K September) also contradicts Luxaire's own style-1 table (K October). Style-6 (11-digit numeric, year/month stated Unknown on the page) is intentionally omitted: no year can be extracted from it, and the page only gives a 1965-1981 company-name window and a contact-the-manufacturer instruction. Luxaire page last updated 2016, older than the York (2024) and Coleman (2023) pages.

styles.era: 8-digit numeric serials (no era dates stated on Luxaire page)
styles.notes: Year first, month second. Same layout as Coleman style-3 but 8 digits and with no era dates stated on the Luxaire page, so no yearFloor override is set.

styles.era: Prior to 1992 (9-digit numeric serials)
styles.notes: Month first, year second. Same layout as Coleman style-4 (page text and chart agree on the 9-digit sample here, unlike Coleman's 9/10-digit discrepancy).

nordyne.notes: Parent company as stated on the page. The page lists related brands (Broan, Frigidaire, Gibson, Intertherm, Kelvinator, Mammoth, Maytag, Miller, NuTone, Philco, Tappan, Westinghouse, Gaz Industrie, Ambirad, Partners Choice, Reznor and private labels) but does not state they share Nordyne's serial system, so no sisters are claimed. No era dates are documented for either style; eras below describe serial shape only. The two styles do not overlap: style-1 is 12 characters, style-2 is 16 characters.

styles.era: 3-letter prefix followed by 9 digits; year and month encoded
styles.notes: Page example shown as GBB03 0708229. Year is the 4th and 5th positions (03, resolving to 2003 under the 1960 floor); month is the 6th and 7th positions (07 = July). Hyphen variants GBB-030708229 and GBB-0307-08229 normalize to the same serial.

styles.era: 16-character serial with a letter-delimited middle section; week and year encoded, no month
styles.notes: Page example shown as MN3D102 F38 91 4228. Week is the 9th and 10th positions (38, the first two digits after the middle-section letter F); year is the 11th and 12th positions (91, the last two digits of that section, resolving to 1991 under the 1960 floor). The page notes this style is similar to Rheem style serials and likely indicates Rheem manufacture for Nordyne; that similarity is not documented verbatim reuse, so usesStylesOf stays null.

payne.notes: BDP system. Styles 1-4 match Bryant styles 1-4 in shape, positions, era, and example serials (style 2, style 3 and style 4 examples are identical serials on both pages). Payne is NOT usesStylesOf Bryant because Payne style 5 differs from Bryant style 5 and Payne lists no Canada variant for style 3. Styles 3-4 letter/digit tables are transcribed from Bryant page text because Payne's own charts are image-only in text fetch; confirm against Payne chart images before treating those tables as Payne-page-confirmed. HELD GAP — style 5 (prior to 1970, 7-digit all-numeric, year = 1st digit): the page shows only the placeholder 6######, which is not a real serial, and the decade mapping lives only in the chart image; no style 5 is shipped rather than guessed. Carrier is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not claimed as sharing this system.

styles.era: 10-character format, week-year in first four digits
styles.notes: Week is 1st-2nd positions, year is 3rd-4th positions. Week decode for the example is 40.

styles.era: 9-character all-numeric
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd positions, month is 3rd-4th positions. Same example serial as Bryant style 2.

Month is 1st position, year digit is 2nd position. Tables transcribed from Bryant page text for the identical BDP system; Payne's own chart is image-only in text fetch. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

Month is 1st position, year digit is 2nd position. Tables transcribed from Bryant page text for the identical BDP system; Payne's own chart is image-only in text fetch. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

reznor.notes: PARTIAL YEAR TABLE for style-1: the page image states the year is coded in the first two or three letters and that year-letter sequences for 1949-2029 are shown in tables below, but those year tables are not present in the fetched page content (only the month table A-L and the single data point BK = 2011, from the Dec 2011 sample, are documented). Style-1 therefore encodes only BK -> 2011; all other style-1 year codes return cannot-determine until the full year table is sourced. The 2-letter key BK is a natural generalization of the letterTable kind to a 2-character slice (the builder looks the slice up exactly); the locked schema prose says single-letter keys, which a future clarification should address. The 2-letter-prefix variant (1-letter year code, per the page tip) is not encoded at all: no year table and no disambiguation rule for it appear in the fetched content, and such serials do not match the style-1 pattern, so they return cannot-determine. Page last updated 2016; parent is as stated on the page.

styles.era: Letter-prefix serials starting with three letters: year is the first two letters, month is the third letter
9-character serials: month is the 1st and 2nd digits, year is the 3rd and 4th digits

rheem.notes: Six documented serial styles. Styles 2-4 share one factory-letter rule (week = 1st and 2nd digits after the factory letter, year = 3rd and 4th digits after it) but are kept as separate styles because the schema positions are absolute and the factory letter sits at a different index in each documented example (index 7, 4, and 5 respectively). Style 5 is described on the page as a common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems; style 6 is an older discontinued style from the mid-1970s and prior, also a water-heater style used on older HVAC systems. Example expected values are derived from the page's stated positions (the page states positions, not printed year values); each derived year is the unique candidate under the 1960 floor and 2026 current year. Ambiguity: the factory letter is described as typically F, M, G, W, or N, so a style 2-4 serial with a non-typical factory letter would fall through to style 5 and mis-decode; ordering (styles 2-4 before style 5) protects only the typical-letter cases. Patterns for styles 2-4 anchor the factory-letter position to the documented example's prefix length; a serial with a different prefix length before the factory letter is not covered and must not be guessed.

styles.era: Letter followed by digits; week and year in the opening digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 4th and 5th positions, week = 2nd and 3rd positions. Normalized W291013412: positions 2-3 = 29 (week), positions 4-5 = 10 (year 2010).

styles.era: Seven-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th numbers following the middle (factory) letter, week = 1st and 2nd numbers following it; factory letter typically F, M, G, W, or N. Normalized CB5D302F099903346: factory letter F at index 7, following digits 09 (week) and 99 (year 1999). Example serial shown on the page with a space (CB5D302F09 9903346); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Four-digit prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized 7351M280616735: factory letter M at index 4, following digits 28 (week) and 06 (year 2006). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (7351 M28 06 16735); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Five-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized OR177M280700097: factory letter M at index 5, following digits 28 (week) and 07 (year 2007). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (OR177 M28 07 00097); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Older HVAC systems; month-year opening digits, also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th positions, month = 1st and 2nd positions; common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems. Normalized 0804B10488: positions 1-2 = 08 (month August), positions 3-4 = 04 (year 2004). Example serial shown on the page with a space (08 04B10488); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Older discontinued style, mid-1970s and prior; also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = last 2 digits, week = 4th and 3rd from last digits (in that order). Normalized 123451872: last 2 digits 72 (year 1972); 4th from last = 1 and 3rd from last = 8, giving week 18. Example serial shown on the page with a space (1234518 72); normalized form strips the space. Limitation: with the default 1960 floor, a genuine pre-1960 style-6 serial (two-digit year below 60) has no valid candidate under the century rule and returns cannot-determine rather than a guessed year; the page gives no start date that would justify a different floor.

ruud.notes: Reuse evidence (page-confirmed, not parent alone): the Ruud page lists the exact same six example serials as the Rheem page (W291013412; CB5D302F09 9903346; 7351 M28 06 16735; OR177 M28 07 00097; 08 04B10488; 1234518 72), with identical position descriptions for year, month, and week, the identical factory-letter note (typically F, M, G, W, or N), and the identical style images (Rheem-HVAC-style-1.jpg through style-6-1.jpg). The Ruud page also states Rheem Manufacturing acquired Ruud in 1959 and Ruud remains a subsidiary of Rheem Manufacturing. The Rheem page lists many other related brands, but only Ruud is verified here as sharing this serial system; no other related brand is claimed as sharing it.

styles.era: Letter followed by digits; week and year in the opening digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 4th and 5th positions, week = 2nd and 3rd positions. Normalized W291013412: positions 2-3 = 29 (week), positions 4-5 = 10 (year 2010).

styles.era: Seven-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits

Normalized CB5D302F099903346: factory letter F at index 7, following digits 09 (week) and 99 (year 1999). Example serial shown on the page with a space (CB5D302F09 9903346); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Four-digit prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized 7351M280616735: factory letter M at index 4, following digits 28 (week) and 06 (year 2006). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (7351 M28 06 16735); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Five-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized OR177M280700097: factory letter M at index 5, following digits 28 (week) and 07 (year 2007). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (OR177 M28 07 00097); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Older HVAC systems; month-year opening digits, also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th positions, month = 1st and 2nd positions; common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems. Normalized 0804B10488: positions 1-2 = 08 (month August), positions 3-4 = 04 (year 2004). Example serial shown on the page with a space (08 04B10488); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Older discontinued style, mid-1970s and prior; also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = last 2 digits, week = 4th and 3rd from last digits (in that order). Normalized 123451872: last 2 digits 72 (year 1972); 4th from last = 1 and 3rd from last = 8, giving week 18. tempstar.notes: ICP system. Sister Keeprite shares styles 1-5 with identical examples and positions, but Keeprite lists no style 6, so no verbatim reuse is claimed in either direction. Style 2 is the same system as style 1 with a printed MFG date on the tag. HELD GAPS — style 4 (8-digit numeric, year = 1st digit, week = 2nd-3rd digits): the format example 30512345 has no stated decode and its year-digit mapping is chart-image-only; styles 5 (letter-digit-letter prefix, year = 3rd letter) and 6 (two-letter prefix, year = 2nd letter): the page shows only placeholders Z3Zxxxxx / ZZxxxxx and the year-letter charts are image-only, and the xxxxx tail shapes are undocumented. None of styles 4-6 is shipped rather than guessed.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits
styles.notes: Year is 2nd-3rd digits, week is 4th-5th digits. Week decode for the example is 16.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits, with printed MFG date on tag
styles.notes: Page states this serial is identical in system to style 1; the printed MFG date 2/92 corroborates year 1992 and week 06. Pattern and positions duplicate style 1, so this style never wins first-match, but its decode is identical.

styles.era: 10-character format, year-week in first four digits
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd digits, week is 3rd-4th digits. Week decode for the example is 14.

trane.notes: Multiple overlapping serial systems; the page advises using data-plate MFR date, ANSI standard date, condition and appearance to disambiguate overlapping styles. Page Style 1 (2002 onward) is documented as used under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names; the page also names GE among brands under which these styles appear. Known-context correction: the page documents the letter-year system from 1983 (not from 1987) through 2001, then the year-first digit system from 2002. Parent per the page header is Ingersoll Rand; the page history notes the 2020 rename to Trane Technologies. HELD, NOT SHIPPED: page Style 7 (8-character serials, documented serial F9190391 with no stated decode; year positions inferred only from similarity to page Style 3) and page Styles 4 (1981-1983, year letter in first or last position depending on product type, ambiguous letter wording), 5 (single-digit year + month letter with no table, decade ambiguous 1970s vs early 1980s), 6 (third-to-last letter year, last two digits week, 1980-1982, no L/M/N letter table), 8 (European; page states it cannot be decoded from any known chart).

styles.era: 2010-present, digit-led serials (page Style 1, later form)
styles.notes: Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2010+ reading) and style-1 (2002-2009 reading); this style is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading. The page notes the styles overlap and directs techs to the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate; a 2002 serial in the overlap set will decode as a 2020s year.

styles.era: 2002-2009, digit-led serials (page Style 1, early form)
styles.notes: Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2002-2009 reading) and style-2 (2010+ reading); style-2 is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate per the page. A 2002 serial in the overlap set therefore decodes as a 2020s year; this is a documented page ambiguity, not a silent guess.

styles.era: 1983-2001, letter-led 9-character serials (page Style 2)
styles.notes: Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: page text says letters A, I, L, O and Q were not used, yet the standard chart reading (corroborated by three independent sources) gives L = 1996; L = 1996 is included pending visual chart verification. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Page states the 4th position encodes month but gives no letter-to-month table (the documented example's 4th character is M), so month is not encoded. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.
